scope: The five existing stock TIE attack/return test failures; no controller or test assertions were changed. This is an immutable working-tree snapshot, not a claim of a full repository test pass.

baseline.scope: The five unchanged stock TIE movement/return cases; the separately powered custom-fighter branch is not selected.
failureNames: a natural bow attack shoots while moving, passes the hull and returns after a finite gun-only sortie
above and below attack runs leave along the hull on their original safe side
an attack that misses its firing window still clears the target and returns
an explicit recall stops firing and docks through the carrier mouth
a fighter initially facing exactly away turns around without a zero heading or zero-speed deadlock

environment.KS_TEST_ROOT: Path to an unchanged export of baselineCommit

nodeArguments: --test-name-pattern=natural bow|above and below|misses its firing|explicit recall|initially facing

method.probeCommandProvenance: Each named temporary probe was run with Node, capturing stdout and stderr. The probes were not added to the repository; their SHA-256 digests identify the exact diagnostic scripts.

poweredStockAircraft.finding: The real stock craft has a positive, nearly fully supplied engine. These movement failures are not evidence of a missing plant, zero thrust, or concurrent output being artificially prevented.

failures.name: a natural bow attack shoots while moving, passes the hull and returns after a finite gun-only sortie
failures.cause: The test expects return within110s; the actual finite-acceleration flight revisits its fixed approach waypoint and makes slow velocity reversals.

failures.name: above and below attack runs leave along the hull on their original safe side
failures.cause: The fixture initializes a2000m/s vertical approach about13km from the target. Its24.9km braking distance exceeds that height; the existing waypoint/controller overshoots and later egress crosses the requested side.

failures.name: an attack that misses its firing window still clears the target and returns
failures.cause: The test replaces R.CRAFT.tie_ln with a spread clone before its lazy power profile is resolved. The clone is not in BUILTIN_CRAFT, so craftPowerOf returnsnull and it drifts without thrust; this is a stale fixture identity assumption.

failures.name: an explicit recall stops firing and docks through the carrier mouth
failures.cause: Recall works and docking finishes, but the current controller chases the gate at nominal speed without anticipatory stopping-distance planning, exceeding the old deadline.

failures.name: a fighter initially facing exactly away turns around without a zero heading or zero-speed deadlock
failures.cause: An initially antiparallel velocity must change with finite acceleration. The old steering controller flips attitude rapidly and brakes/reverses velocity through a low speed, violating the test minimum-speed assumption.

conclusion: Four failures expose old high-speed AI timing/steering assumptions under finite acceleration; one uses an unpowered cloned craft fixture. Stock aircraft can attack, return and dock, but the old short deadlines and high-speed safe-side/no-slowdown guarantees do not hold. Controller redesign was not undertaken and assertions were not weakened.
sourceRelation: Measured at the recorded working-tree source hashes before the final frozen-source regression run. These timings are diagnostic evidence, not assertions rerun against the final sources.
